p010-u001: RoboMaster teams must develop and build their robots themselves. Participating robots must satisfy all specifications described in this document, and Pre-Match Inspection staff will spot-check robots according to its provisions. Robots must also comply with relevant laws and regulations and must not pose safety hazards. If a violation causes a safety accident, RMOC will pursue the violating party's legal liability in accordance with the law. If there is any dispute over these specifications, the interpretation of the Chief Referee or Chief Inspector shall prevail.
p010-u004: Provisions marked “S#” before an item (for example, S10) are mandatory provisions. They focus on key requirements such as safety, size/weight, electromagnetic compatibility, and field rules, and must be strictly observed. For a violation, RMOC may refuse the robot's participation, require rectification by a deadline, or directly disqualify it, depending on the nature of the violation.
p010-u006: Provisions not marked “S#” are advisory. They are intended to optimize performance, improve stability, or reduce failure risk, but are not hard conditions for passing Pre-Match Inspection. Failure to follow an advisory provision does not directly affect inspection approval, but may cause module malfunction, limited performance during matches, additional repair/damage-assessment costs, or safety hazards. The team bears all resulting losses and consequences.
p010-u007: Unless a provision states otherwise, all mandatory provisions in this manual apply to both RMUC and RMUL robots. RMUL robots may be exempt from a specific requirement if the relevant robot type, field prop, or competition rule does not apply to RMUL.

p022-u007: Sufficient redesign means improving a robot’s core mechanism in a way that has broad effects on related systems.
p022-u011: Change in wheel-group configuration, such as changing among mecanum wheels, steering wheels, omni wheels, Ackermann steering wheels, or tracks;
p022-u013: Change in the wheel-group transmission configuration, such as moving the drive source from unsprung to sprung mass, or vice versa;
p022-u015: Change in suspension configuration, such as changing among double-wishbone, torsion-beam, double-longitudinal-arm, or lift suspension;
p022-u017: Change in chassis drive, such as changing between DC and AC, brushed and brushless, geared and direct drive;
p022-u019: Change in chassis form, such as changing among frame-type, layered-plate, and unibody chassis.
p022-u023: Change in the Gimbal’s transmission stack, such as changing the inclusion relationships or number of the Yaw, Pitch, and Roll axes;
p022-u025: Change in the projectile-feeding principle, such as changing from a simple direct feed path to feeding through the Yaw-axis joint to the launching mechanism;
p022-u027: Change in the magazine location, such as changing whether it is fixed to the chassis, Yaw axis, or Pitch axis;
p022-u029: Change in the Gimbal motor transmission method, such as changing among direct drive, belts, linkages, and gears (excluding swapping belts, gears, and sprockets for one another).
p023-u003: Change in the topology of mechanisms other than the end effector, such as changing the order, number, or type of revolute and prismatic joints;
p023-u005: Improve actuator power efficiency, for example, by reducing the number of power sources with function unchanged, or increasing effective function while keeping or increasing the number of power sources.
p023-u009: Dart body: Change the overall aerodynamic configuration or the method of generating control forces. For example, change from a conventional main-wing-and-tail layout to a flying-wing layout;
p023-u010: or substantially restructure the function allocation of the front and rear aerodynamic control surfaces, with corresponding redesign of the aerodynamic layout, actuators, and control coordination.
p023-u012: Dart Launcher: Change the principle of the launching power or the topology of the core transmission; change the kinematic-chain topology of the core feeding or loading mechanism.
p023-u013: For example, change from elastic-energy ejection to friction-wheel acceleration; redesign the drive kinematic chain so the principle by which power is input, transmitted, and applied to the Dart changes.
p023-u017: Hangar: Change the principle or kinematic-chain topology of the core storage, transfer, or docking mechanism. For example, change from independently parking and launching at each bay to a shared launch platform with an active transfer mechanism; or change from fixed passive-guided docking to active multi-axis alignment, with corresponding restructuring of sensing, actuation, and control.
p023-u019: Aerial Robot: Change the overall arrangement of lift units or the principle of the attitude-control mechanism; change the main load-bearing structure. For example, change from coplanar rotors to coaxial placement, or from fixed-axis rotors to actively tilting rotors, thereby changing how loads transfer among power units, onboard equipment, and landing structures.
p023-u021: Non-sufficient redesign means an improvement with limited effects on related systems.
p023-u023: A change of more than 10% in a key parameter (such as suspension hardpoint position, track width, wheelbase, Dart Launcher effective acceleration stroke, Dart body, or local Aerial Robot aerodynamic geometry);
p023-u025: Change in the number of effective powered wheel groups;
p023-u027: Change in chassis, Gimbal, Dart Launcher, or Hangar drive-motor gear ratio, or in an actuator’s local transmission path or method;
p023-u029: Change the placement orientation of at least three onboard Referee System modules, with each change causing a topology change in the robot system;
p023-u031: Add a new functional module related to the robot’s existing functions, such as an independent rescue device, small video-transmission gimbal, Energy Unit orientation mechanism, or vision module; Dart Launcher loading or launching modules; or Aerial System/Dart-body sensing, feedback, or actuation modules.
p023-u033: Change between longitudinal and transverse friction-wheel placement;
p024-u001: Change the power source, for example, pneumatic to electric;
p024-u003: Change the end-effector type or configuration, for example, rotary grasping to translational grasping;
p024-u005: Change the layout of core electronic components (main controller, power supply, computing platform, sensing modules), for example, move them from the Gimbal to the chassis;
p024-u007: Change the Gimbal’s rotation range from limited to unlimited;
p024-u009: Adjust the size, number, or mounting angle of local aerodynamic components on the Dart, such as tail area, tail mounting angle, or airfoil camber;
p024-u011: Change the Dart material and adjust its mass distribution or surface properties;
p024-u013: Adjust the layout or structure of the Dart Launcher feeding mechanism, such as changing the shape of the feed track or optimizing the projectile pusher shape;
p024-u015: Revise the transmission ratio or path between Dart Launcher components.
p024-u017: Invalid redesign means a modification that has little effect on core functions.
p024-u018: Invalid redesign includes, but is not limited to, the following modifications:
p024-u020: Modify non-primary load-bearing structures or cover/guard structures, such as changing perforations or shape;
p024-u022: Change the quantity or model of standard parts;
p024-u024: Swap a pneumatic cylinder for an electric pushrod;
p024-u026: Routine counterweight adjustment, changing only the servo or battery model, or changing only the mounting interface that mates with the launching mechanism;
p024-u028: Substitute materials with the same characteristics, such as swapping fiberglass and carbon-fiber plates;
p024-u030: Make a change without changing the principle, such as changing a rigid upper feed tube to a soft tube;
p024-u032: Change only the Hangar outer case or hatch shape while copying the same parking bays;
p024-u034: For an Aerial Robot, change only the propellers, motors, battery, or flight-controller model; change only PID or off-the-shelf firmware settings; or add only a non-primary load-bearing propeller guard;
p024-u036: For a Dart Launcher, change only the motor, spring, or rubber-band specification, or change only the shell or Dart mounting method.
p024-u038: S65 Unless otherwise specified, teams must not use third-party finished modules or finished systems when building robots.
